post.summary:
Exchanges the single-use secret from a sign-in link for a bearer token, activating an invited
user

post.description:
Authenticated, unlike invitation redemption: the credential being renewed is the one the
request carries, so a client whose token has already expired signs in again rather than
refreshing.
post.summary: Swaps the token on this request for a fresh one, restarting its lifetime

delete.summary: Signs out, on this device and every other

get.summary: Returns the profile behind the bearer token on this request

delete.summary: Deletes an organization along with its users

get.description: Behind the bearer token like everything else here, because which organizations exist is not public. A browser cannot put a token on an ``, so a client fetches this and hands the response to the element as an object URL.
get.summary: Returns the organization's logo, or the placeholder when it has none

put.summary: Sets or replaces the organization's logo, and answers with the organization

delete.summary: Removes the organization's logo, which puts it back to the placeholder

get.summary:
Returns a page of users, optionally limited to those still invited or already active.
Deleted users are left out unless `includeDeleted` asks for them, which is how an
administrator finds one to restore

put.summary: Updates the signed-in user's own profile. Open to any role, unlike the administrator edit

get.summary: Returns a single user. Deleted users are not found here; the roster lists them on request

put.summary:
Updates a user's name, email address, role and organization, as an administrator. Omitting
`role` or `organizationId` leaves that field alone, which is the whole request an
organization administrator can make: changing either is reserved to platform administrators

delete.summary:
Deletes a user. They lose access immediately and are emailed about it; an administrator can
undo this with the restore endpoint

post.summary:
Invites somebody into an organization and emails them a link that accepts the invitation and
signs them in
Sends a fresh invitation link, retiring the previous one

Restores a deleted user, leaving one who is not deleted as they are. Their sign-in links and
sessions are not restored with them, so they sign in again from the login page

logoUrl.description:
Always populated, and always answers: an organization with no uploaded logo is served
the placeholder, so a client has one address to point at rather than a branch and a
copy of the fallback image. `hasLogo` is for a client that needs to tell the two
apart, such as one offering to replace an image that is really there.

UpdateOwnProfileRequest.description: A user's own edit. The name and nothing else.
UpdateOwnProfileRequest.title: UpdateOwnProfileRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
An administrator's edit.

`role` and `organizationId` are optional and mean "leave this alone"; the fields every editor can
change are always sent.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UploadOrganizationLogoRequest.description:
The logo upload.

Both of the upload's own rejections are stated here, so the API answers them the same way whether
the caller sent one byte too many or a file that is not an image at all: a 400 naming the field.

The format is checked by reading the bytes, never by believing the upload's `Content-Type` or its
file name. The stored value is what a later response is labelled with, so a media type nothing
verified would be one an attacker chose.
UploadOrganizationLogoRequest.title: UploadOrganizationLogoRequest

invitationExpiresUtc.description:
Read off the outstanding invitation rather than worked out from `invitedUtc` and the
configured lifetime: the link's expiry was fixed when it was issued, so reconfiguring
that lifetime cannot retroactively expire or revive one. At most one invitation is
outstanding per user, because issuing a new one retires the last.

UserRole.description:
The capabilities a user has. Roles are hierarchical: every higher role includes the rights of the lower ones, which is what {@see self::atLeast()} expresses. The backing values are the names the API has always used, so a stored row and a token claim read the same as the JSON a client receives. | | |---| | `Member`
Can read their own organization and the people in it. | | `Administrator`
Can invite, update and remove users within their own organization, and rename it. | | `PlatformAdministrator`
Can manage every organization and every user in the system. |
UserRole.title: UserRole

UserStatus.description:
Where a user is in the invitation lifecycle. Deliberately separate from deletion, which is recorded by its own timestamp: the status says how far somebody got, and overwriting it on delete would lose the answer a restore has to put back. | | |---| | `Invited`
Invited, but has not yet signed in for the first time. | | `Active`
Has proven ownership of their email address and can sign in. |
UserStatus.title: UserStatus

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
